## Split one workbook into several

A model declares fixed-cell metadata, table layouts, primary keys, and parent keys.
The caller supplies a structurally validated source workbook and an empty template for the same model version.

The bundled survey model has a composite primary key `[station, observation_id]` on `Observations`.
Each output contains one observation and all fixed metadata, even when identifiers repeat across stations.

```{r split, eval=FALSE}
library(form.tools)
examples <- system.file("examples", package = "form.model")
model <- form.model::load_form_model("survey", examples)
outputs <- split_form_workbook(
  file.path(examples, "survey.xlsx"), model,
  root_sheet = "Observations",
  template = file.path(examples, "survey-empty.xlsx"),
  directory = "survey-by-observation",
  shared_sheets = "Equipment"
)
outputs
```

Output filenames retain the original basename and append the root primary-key values in model order.
For example, `survey.xlsx` with key `[ST01, OBS-001]` produces `survey_ST01_OBS-001.xlsx`.
Invalid filename characters become `_`; case-insensitive collisions and names exceeding 255 bytes are rejected.
The returned manifest maps each file to its source row and primary-key components.
Root key values are never interpreted as filesystem paths.

## Shared data

Fixed-cell model fields are copied into every output workbook.
Template sheets outside the model remain unchanged.
Source sheets outside the model are not copied.

The survey example copies the independent `Equipment` table with `shared_sheets = "Equipment"`.

All tables outside the selected hierarchy must be declared shared; the tool never silently drops such tables.

## Template requirements

The model and both workbooks must agree on worksheet names and physical layouts.
The caller selects the exact template version. Both workbooks must use the same Excel date system.

Table data regions must contain no values or formulas.
Prepare the first data row with the desired column styles and row height for additional records.
Existing styled rows are retained. Standard validation and conditional-formatting ranges are extended as needed.

Excel tables and merged cells in template data regions are not supported.
Fixed print areas and extended Excel validation ranges are preserved without expansion.

## Validation and publication

The source must already pass structural validation.
The splitter also checks required sheets, extents, complete and unique primary keys, and existing parent keys.
Other field and business-rule findings do not prevent splitting.

Source formulas contribute cached values only. Excel errors and formulas without caches in modeled fields are rejected.
Template formulas outside modeled fields are retained; the output requests recalculation when opened in Excel.
R does not recalculate formulas.

The output directory must be new, with an existing parent directory.
All output files are prepared before the directory is published; failures leave no partial output directory.
Neither the input workbook nor the template is modified.
